source.title: "Deep lifts": Neural networks can generalize even with the dumbest optimizer

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper body, appendices and references; it is not visibly garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes generalization of uniformly sampled parameters conditioned on interpolation, including under label corruptions. This bears conceptually on noisy-label generalization, but it does not train standard networks with SGD or test the original random-label fitting setup.
record.gate_note: The paper defines its learner to sample only parameters that interpolate the observed labels. Theorems about corrupted labels report generalization bounds for that learner. The introduction's statement that deep networks can fit random labels cites Zhang et al. (2017), so it is not this study's result. No experiments or observed training-error results are reported.
record.test_reason: The learner is conditioned on interpolation; the study analyzes its population risk rather than whether training produces random-label fitting. Its corruption-dependent upper bounds do not establish steadily increasing test error or chance error at full corruption. The random-label fitting statement is attributed to Zhang et al. (2017). No claim version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: deep lifting extends generalization guarantees for uniform random interpolators to continuous weights and label noise, isolating architectural contributions from optimizer bias. The authors identify the unrealistic learning rule as the principal limitation. Their guarantees do not establish empirical smooth degradation or a positive noise-induced risk floor.
record.recipe_differences: The study samples uniformly from parameters conditioned on interpolation rather than training with SGD or another stochastic gradient method. The results are theoretical guarantees, not a reproduction of the original experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The bounds depend on the corruption count or rate, architecture width and depth, and assumptions on the witness, weight bound and input distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 6/37 bound population interpolation risk by a term proportional to W(wD+m) log(q_eff,n)/n, with confidence terms, for uniformly sampled interpolators under witness, distribution, width, and weight-bound assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uniformly sampled ReLU interpolators can have controlled population risk despite bounded adversarial label corruption when a small network approximates the underlying signal.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 40 bounds risk by Õ(W(1+w/B)ϵ) at a specified sample size and chosen depth under binomial corruption counts. This is an upper guarantee, not a demonstrated nonzero error floor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At selected sample sizes and architecture scalings, uniform random interpolators admit population-risk upper bounds proportional to the label-corruption rate.

record.problems: The authors call the learning rule unrealistic. The noisy-label findings are theoretical bounds under explicit witness, distribution and architecture assumptions; they do not provide empirical random-label training results or a measured test-error curve.
record.rows_left_out: No other qualifying result rows identified. The introduction's discussion of fitting randomly assigned labels is attributed to Zhang et al. (2017), not reported as a result of this study.

untested.parts: SGD fitting completely random labels, near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time comparisons and convergence slowdown with increasing corruption.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect fitting arising through training throughout a random-label corruption sweep, with actual test error increasing steadily toward chance while retaining signal.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, and their removal.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noise.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V4 limits_scope verdict: untested components are not scope limitations. Appendix H also analyzes uniform and interpolation-conditioned Boltzmann classifiers, but likewise provides risk bounds with interpolation imposed, so it adds no qualifying claim-version result.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train standard networks with stochastic gradient methods on completely random labels, or test chance test error or unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
No training-time comparison or convergence-speed measurement.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments.

The analysis gives theoretical risk bounds for uniformly sampled interpolators under bounded adversarial label corruption. It does not report a smooth empirical test-error curve from zero to all corrupted labels, establish chance error at full corruption, or measure capture of remaining signal.
Does not test weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.
Does not compare learning of real and random labels over training time.

rows.note: The learner is conditioned by definition to interpolate the corrupted training labels. This is a bound, not an observed error rate or a sweep showing steady degradation.
rows.check: Theorem 6 bounds population regression risk for parameters sampled conditional on interpolation under bounded adversarial corruption. An upper bound increasing with corruption count does not establish V4's actual test-error trajectory. Interpolation is imposed, and architecture requirements depend on corruption count. Retain only as a theoretical result outside these versions.
